issues.display_title: Issue #389: Refactor Report Query Result Handling
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 14/07/26

✅ Implementation: Report Query Result Refactoring

This document tracks the execution details for the report query result refactoring.

Phase 1: ReportComment Lookup

  • Target File: src/Action/V1/Report/ReportComment.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added a local reportCommentTarget struct with explicit id and visibility GORM column mappings.
    • Replaced var comment map[string]interface{} with var comment reportCommentTarget.
    • Replaced Scan(&comment) with Take(&comment).
    • Added explicit gorm.ErrRecordNotFound handling for missing comments.
    • Replaced map type assertions with typed field access.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 2: ReportPost Lookup

  • Target File: src/Action/V1/Report/ReportPost.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added a local reportPostTarget struct with explicit id, visibility, and user_id GORM column mappings.
    • Replaced var post map[string]interface{} with var post reportPostTarget.
    • Replaced Scan(&post) with Take(&post).
    • Added explicit gorm.ErrRecordNotFound handling for missing posts.
    • Replaced map type assertions with typed field access.
    • Preserved blocked-user filtering and private-post validation.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 3: UpdateReportBug Debug Log Cleanup

  • Target File: src/Action/V1/Report/UpdateReportBug.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Removed fmt.Println(accountSupport).
    • Removed the unused fmt import.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Verification

  • Ran go test ./src/Action/V1/Report.
  • Result: passed with no test files.

Background

The report endpoints used map[string]interface{} for joined lookup queries in ReportComment and ReportPost. This made the code depend on runtime type assertions for database fields. UpdateReportBug also contained a support-account debug print that could leak configuration values into logs.

Objective

Refactor the small report query lookups to use typed result structs and remove unnecessary debug logging while preserving endpoint behavior.

Scope

  • Replace map[string]interface{} comment lookup result handling in ReportComment.
  • Replace map[string]interface{} post lookup result handling in ReportPost.
  • Use Take and explicit gorm.ErrRecordNotFound handling for missing report targets.
  • Preserve private post/comment validation and existing response messages.
  • Remove the support account debug print from UpdateReportBug.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ReportComment no longer reads the comment lookup into map[string]interface{}.
  • ReportPost no longer reads the post lookup into map[string]interface{}.
  • Missing comment and post targets still return existing conflict responses.
  • UpdateReportBug no longer prints ACCOUNT_SP values.
  • Verification passes with:
go test ./src/Action/V1/Report

issues.display_title: Issue #390: Refactor Support Category Queries to Use GORM Models
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 14/07/26

✅ # Implementation: Support Category GORM Refactoring

This document tracks the execution details for the support category GORM refactoring.

Phase 1: Support Categories

  • Target Files:
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/AddSupportCategory.go
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/UpdateSupportCategory.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added the Models import.
    • Removed the local categoryRow struct from AddSupportCategory.
    • Replaced Config.DB.Table("categories") count, create, and update operations with Config.DB.Model(&Models.Categories{}) or Config.DB.Create(&Models.Categories{}).
    • Replaced the raw max-id query with a model-based select for COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) + 1.
    • Preserved existing validation, duplicate-name checks, and response payloads.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 2: Affiliate Categories

  • Target Files:
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/AddAffiliateCategory.go
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/UpdateAffiliateCategory.go
    • src/Models/AffiliateCategories.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added the Models import.
    • Removed the local affiliateCategoryRow struct from AddAffiliateCategory.
    • Added Position to Models.AffiliateCategories.
    • Replaced Config.DB.Table("affiliate_categories") count, create, and update operations with Config.DB.Model(&Models.AffiliateCategories{}) or Config.DB.Create(&Models.AffiliateCategories{}).
    • Replaced the raw max-position query with a model-based select for COALESCE(MAX(position), 0) + 1.
    • Preserved existing duplicate-name, affiliate-usage, and response behavior.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Verification

  • Ran go test ./src/Action/V1/Supports.
  • Result: passed with no test files.

Background

The support category endpoints used direct table access and small local row structs for category creation and updates. These endpoints can use the existing model layer instead, keeping support category operations aligned with the wider GORM refactor.

Objective

Refactor support and affiliate category endpoints to use GORM models for category count, create, and update operations.

Scope

  • Refactor AddSupportCategory to use Models.Categories.
  • Refactor UpdateSupportCategory to use Models.Categories.
  • Refactor AddAffiliateCategory to use Models.AffiliateCategories.
  • Refactor UpdateAffiliateCategory to use Models.AffiliateCategories.
  • Add any missing model fields needed by the category endpoints.
  • Preserve existing response messages and validation behavior.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Local category row structs are removed where existing models can represent the table.
  • Support category create/update operations use Models.Categories.
  • Affiliate category create/update operations use Models.AffiliateCategories.
  • Existing duplicate-name and not-found checks remain in place.
  • Verification passes with:
go test ./src/Action/V1/Supports
